chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Expected to sing 'Loch Lomond' and a disc jockey's help
summary: She was expected to do her hits and a Washington disc jockey played her records.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: And I guess the opportunity of maybe redefining yourself into a jazz singer and doing maybe the kinds of things you've been doing now for the past ten years didn't present itself at that time?

Not really because I was expected to do the "Loch Lomand"/and "Molly Malone" which were very good to me. In fact, after I had been retired for about ten years, this is when I got the call in 1967 from Tommy Cotney. He asked me to come down and work at Blues Alley. And of course Tommy had known nothing about me but what caused him to call me was the fact that Felix "If I Had A Ribbon Bow"

Grant was a disc jockey down in Washington D.C., and he was playing my records, "If I Had A Ribbon Bow". And he had never heard it before and he was interested and he called me and asked me if I was interested in working at "The Blues Alley" and I told him look, I haven't sung in over ten years. And we had gone through the Rock era of things and I was actually afraid to open my mouth in public. So I said I was tied up and wasn't able to get away. So he said, I'll call you around June and see what you're doing. So he called. He called and said: "You opened July the 12th." So I did "If I Had A Ribbon" and all those other things from the other material I had and it went well. But I still wasn't decided that I would get back into show business. That was just one engagement and it was a nice feeling and all that.
